page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head at the top, left of centre, with the page number at the top right. Section heading "SECT. IIII." centred in the middle of the page. Signature "P 4" at the foot left, below the last line. No margin notes.

main_text.l: Quisquis ergo vendicat sibi jus dispen-
sandi in Juramento, assumit sibi pote-
statem divinam, erigendo sibi tribunal
in foro interno, & exercendo dominium
in hominum conscientias. Et est ipsa
dispensatio invalida, & de jure nulla: s-
icut sententia prolata a Judice in loro [?]
non suo, quia prolata est a non Ju-
dice, est ad omnem juris effectum invalida.
SECT. IIII.
Torquent hic se mirum in modum
Dispensationum Patroni, ut primi argu-
menti (quod sibimet unum objicere so-
lent) vim declinare videantur. Sudant
nimirum hoc saxum versando, (tuen-
dam enim sibi vident utcunque Papæ
hac ex parte authoritatem, ne culinæ suæ
male sit) nec tamen proficiunt hilum:
dum quo se solide tueantur non habent,
nec inter ipsos adhuc unquam convenire
potuit, quo jure Papa hanc sibi arroget
dispensandi potestatem. Quod vel u-
num malæ defensionis conscientiam ar-
guit. Quemadmodum enim in bello
suscipiendo, sic & in exercenda pote-
state, causa quæ parum constanter assig-
natur, facile præsumitur esse parum
justa.

page.notes: The word "objicere" is struck through by a stroke in the print. "loro" in the sentence "in loro non suo" is doubtful; it may be a printing error for "loco" or similar, and is marked [?]. The page's first line is a continuation from the previous page. The last line "justa." sits beside the signature "P 4". The "s" long s is rendered as plain s throughout.
